description: A reserved word after `.` / `?.` is a member name: struct fields named `server`, `fn`, `if`, `for`, `of` are read through chains (`t.server.id`, `t?.server.id`, `t.fn.on`). sum(t) = 10 + 20 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 36; pick(t) = 10; pick(not) = 0 — @total is 46 after the click, and @flag is "on" (t.server.on is true, t.fn.on is false).
rationale: §7.2: "All JavaScript that is valid in a Bun execution context is valid inside `${ }`, except the constructs §7.2.1 excludes" — in JavaScript a member name is any IdentifierName, reserved words included. §7.2.1: "`class` SHALL remain valid … as a member name (`x.class`, `x?.class`) … A diagnostic on any of these is a compiler defect." The bootstrap lexed the `.id` after `t.server` as a bare variant and ended the statement there (E-STMT-MISSING-SEMICOLON).
